landmark_student_caveat.implication: run12's INPUT FEATURES are computed by a landmark student whose own training set is 38.8% ASL-Citizen frames. So although the run12 recognizer never touches AC sign data, the shipped SimCC student ONNX is AC-INFLUENCED at the geometry level (it learned hand-coordinate prediction partly from AC frames).
landmark_student_caveat.honest_reading_of_the_AC_constraint: ASL Citizen's noncommercial license constrains the DATA and models DERIVED FROM the data. The student is a model derived (in part) from AC frames, even though it only outputs geometry, not labels. A strict reading therefore says: run12 RECOGNIZER weights are PopSign-only and clean, but the END-TO-END shipped pipeline (student ONNX + recognizer) still contains an AC-derived component. A conservative 'truly distributable, zero AC derivation anywhere in the shipped graph' claim is NOT yet met by (A) alone.
